member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Plugin.Acad.AcadDispatcher
member.summary:
Runs code on AutoCAD's main thread, in the application context, for callers on any thread (the pipe server answers the MCP bridge on thread-pool threads; the AutoCAD API is single-threaded).
Mechanism (AutoCAD 2027, .NET 10). Work items are posted to the WPF of AutoCAD's main thread, captured in (IExtensionApplication.Initialize runs on the main thread). AutoCAD's main window, ribbon and palettes are hosted on that thread, and every Win32 message loop that runs there (the idle main loop, and the nested loops while a command waits for input) dispatches the dispatcher's posted message. An item therefore starts like a palette button click: from the message loop, in the application context, within milliseconds, without the user moving the mouse. While an item runs, is a of the same dispatcher, so every await inside an asynchronous item resumes on the main thread, also while a command is active and waiting for input (which is what typing command input with Document.SendStringToExecute and then awaiting the next prompt needs).
Why not the alternatives. DocumentCollection.ExecuteInApplicationContext is called from a command (on the main thread) to leave the document context, so it does not solve the hop from a background thread. Application.Idle is raised by AutoCAD's idle processing after messages have been handled: a queue drained from Idle needs a wake-up message when AutoCAD is completely idle, and AutoCAD does not document that Idle is raised while a command waits for input, which typing command input step by step depends on. AutoCAD's own Autodesk.AutoCAD.Runtime.SynchronizationContext is installed on the main thread but its scheduling is not documented. The main thread's WPF dispatcher is documented .NET behaviour and is what AutoCAD's WPF palettes and the ribbon run on. still exposes Idle as an "AutoCAD has caught up" signal.
Busy. An item does not start while a modal dialog is open in AutoCAD (AutoCAD's main window is disabled while any modal dialog or message box is shown); it waits for the dialog to close. An item that has not started within fails with . Code already on the main thread runs inline. Once started, synchronous items cannot be interrupted; asynchronous items should honour their cancellation token.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Plugin.Drafting.DraftingEngine
member.summary:
Types AutoCAD commands and their inputs into the command line VISIBLY, one input at a time, the way a drafter types (the heart of run_commands). Runs on AutoCAD's main thread inside : every await resumes on the main thread in the application context.
Mechanism (chosen for AutoCAD 2027 after comparing the options). Each command and each input is sent with Document.SendStringToExecute(text + "\n", activate: true, wrapUpInactiveDoc: false, echoCommand: true), exactly like keyboard input: AutoCAD echoes it in the command line ("Specify first point: 0,0"), validates it like typed input, and draws the result before the next input is sent. After each input the engine yields to AutoCAD's message loop and polls (30 ms) until AutoCAD has taken the input: a new prompt started (Editor.PromptingForXxx), the command ended/cancelled/failed, AutoCAD became quiescent, or the queued input is gone (Internal.Utils.IsInputPending) and the state changed. Only then, after the watch-mode pause (), is the next input typed. This keeps every input visible and gives the engine a clean point to check the prompt, the command-line messages and the command state between inputs.
Why not Editor.CommandAsync inside DocumentCollection.ExecuteInCommandContextAsync. It passes all arguments of a command in one call like AutoLISP's (command), shows them only through CMDECHO, cannot pause between arguments, cannot see which prompt each argument met or which one AutoCAD rejected, and leaves surplus arguments to the Command prompt. SendStringToExecute is the documented way for modeless UI to type into AutoCAD, and the only one that looks like a person typing.
Safety. The plan was checked by and approved before the engine starts. While typing: an input is never typed when its command has already ended (it would start another command at the Command prompt); an input containing a space or ';' is typed only at a text prompt (elsewhere a space acts like Enter and would split it); TEXTEVAL=0 keeps "(" literal at text prompts; and vetoes any forbidden command AutoCAD is about to run. Dialogs are switched off (); one that still opens is cancelled () and the call stops with its title. The user's Esc stops the call.
Self-healing (run_commands autoFix, default on; rules in , pure and unit-tested): before an input is typed, typographic marks and spaces in coordinates are fixed ("10, 20" -> "10,20"); when AutoCAD rejects an input and asks again, one syntax-only retry is typed at the same prompt (feet-inches or mm/m in drawing units, option keyword typos -> capital letters, degree signs removed); a step still waiting at a finish prompt after its inputs gets the forgotten Enter (at most ); a command that still opens a dialog box is retyped as its '-' version. Every fix is reported (StepReport.AutoFixed, "Auto-fixed: ..." in the summary); nothing that changes the meaning of the geometry is ever guessed.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Plugin.Drafting.SysvarScope
member.summary:
The system variables a run_commands call sets so typed input means exactly what the classic command line means, and always restores. Main thread only.
SYSMON = 0the system-variable monitor prints no "**** System Variable Changed ****" notices into the command line the engine reads (the settings below and the AI's own SETVARs would trigger them).
CMDDIA, FILEDIA, ATTDIA = 0commands prompt on the command line instead of opening dialogs (plot, file names, attribute values).
TEXTED = 1TEXT takes its text on the command line instead of the in-place editor.
TEXTEVAL = 0text answers starting with "(" or "!" are taken literally, never evaluated as AutoLISP.
DYNPICOORDS = 1with Dynamic Input on, "10,0" stays absolute and only "@10,0" is relative.
OSNAPCOORD = 1typed coordinates win over running object snaps.
NOMUTT = 0prompts and messages are shown (the user watches them, the engine reads them).
PICKAUTO = 0a typed point that hits nothing at "Select objects:" selects nothing instead of starting a window.
PICKADD 0 -> 2several picks add up instead of replacing each other.
The original values are also written to %LOCALAPPDATA%\AcadCopilot\drafting-sysvars.json until they are restored, so a crash of AutoCAD in the middle of a call cannot leave the user's registry settings (FILEDIA, CMDDIA...) changed: the next call puts them back first.

member.summary:
"Click to point" and "select and ask" inside AutoCAD (one instance per AutoCAD session, created on the main thread with ).
Picking from a modeless palette. The palette's buttons and the copilot's dispatcher items run in AutoCAD's application context, where Editor.GetPoint cannot prompt (it needs a command). The pick therefore runs inside DocumentCollection.ExecuteInCommandContextAsync (AutoCAD 2016+, accoremgd; verified by reflection in AutoCAD 2027: ExecutionResult ExecuteInCommandContextAsync(Func<object, Task>, object), awaitable), which runs the callback like a command of the active drawing: GetPoint shows its prompt in the command line, the user clicks (object snaps, ortho and transparent zoom/pan work), Enter finishes a multi-point pick and Esc cancels. Keyboard focus is moved to the drawing first (Internal.Utils.SetFocusToDwgView through ). A time limit or the panel's Cancel presses Esc for the user (, typed input that the waiting GetPoint takes as a cancel). Points come back in world coordinates (UCS -> WCS).
Selection. Follows Document.ImpliedSelectionChanged (and the end of commands) of the active drawing, debounced, and reads the pickfirst set with Editor.SelectImplied; the first objects are described with . The last non-empty selection is kept for get_selection ("last").

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Plugin.Recovery.CheckpointService
member.summary:
Checkpoints of open drawings (create_checkpoint, list_checkpoints, restore_checkpoint, run_commands' autoCheckpoint).
Design (chosen after comparing the options). A checkpoint is TWO things:
An AutoCAD UNDO mark (_.UNDO _Mark, typed like the user would). Restoring types _.UNDO _Back once per mark placed since then. This is exact: AutoCAD's own undo puts back every object with its handle, every layer, style and setting, and paper space. It lives only while the drawing stays open in this AutoCAD session, and marks are anonymous, so the copilot keeps the stack of marks it placed () with a fingerprint of the drawing at each (entities by handle, layer count). After EVERY Back the drawing must match the expected fingerprint; if it does not (the user undid past a mark, placed own marks, or undo was reset) the Backs are reversed with REDO/MREDO and the restore stops, so nothing is lost. When no mark is left AutoCAD asks "This will undo everything. OK?" and the copilot answers No.
A copy of the drawing (Database.Wblock() = WBLOCK *, saved with Database.SaveAs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\AcadCopilot\checkpoints\<drawing>\, never the user's file, at most 20 per drawing, deleted after 7 days). It survives closing or crashing AutoCAD. Restoring from it (fromFile) erases the model-space objects and inserts the copy's model space (Database.Insert): the geometry comes back, handles change, and layouts, layers and styles of the current drawing stay as they are (only missing ones are added). Because that is less exact, it is only used when asked for explicitly, and a checkpoint of the current state is taken first.
Rejected alternatives: copying handles and properties of model-space objects (misses table records, dictionaries, paper space, and cannot recreate erased objects faithfully); reopening the copy as the drawing (would close the user's document). Everything here runs on AutoCAD's main thread inside the dispatcher.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Plugin.Tools.ToolRegistry
member.summary:
All AutoCAD tools of the plug-in, exposed over the pipe (tools.list / tools.call) and through the MCP bridge. The tools are contributed by partial methods in the other ToolRegistry.*.cs files:
ToolRegistry.Drafting.cs (drafting agent): run_commands, cancel_command, undo.
ToolRegistry.Inspect.cs (vision agent): get_drawing_info, capture_view, list_layers, list_entities, get_entity, get_sysvars.
ToolRegistry.Learning.cs: learn_style_from_drawing (the other learning tools are answered by the MCP bridge).
Names must be unique, valid () and must not use the bridge's reserved names (ask_user, update_plan, acad_status); definitions must pass .
Drafting tools (run_commands, cancel_command, undo), followed by the recovery tools (ToolRegistry.Recovery.cs).

Inspection tools, all read-only (Risk Read, read transactions, no document lock): get_drawing_info, capture_view, list_layers, list_entities, get_entity and get_sysvars. The last five are defined in ; the work is done by , , and .

Tools that involve the user's hands in the drawing (Plugin/Interaction, ):
pick_point: asks the user to click one or more points (prompt in the command line and the panel).
get_selection: the objects the user selected (or selected last), with summaries.
select_objects: selects and highlights objects by handle so the user sees them.
pick_point and select_objects have risk Write only so that they take a turn in AutoCAD like typing does (one command line); they never change the drawing. Compile-verified only (the handlers need AutoCAD).

Learning tools of the plug-in: learn_style_from_drawing (reads the active drawing on AutoCAD's main thread, analyses it with and merges the result into style.md). The other learning tools (remember_rule, save_recipe, save_lesson, recall_knowledge, forget) only touch the knowledge files and are answered by the MCP bridge itself (), so they never wait for AutoCAD.
Recovery tools (create_checkpoint, list_checkpoints, restore_checkpoint, get_resume_info).

Services and presentation tools: insert_symbol_library and place_services_legend (electrical / plumbing first-draft layouts), fill_presentation_regions and add_presentation_backdrop (colour presentation elevation) and export_view_png (a shareable PNG). Definitions live in AcadCopilot.Core (Services/, Presentation/), the AutoCAD work in Plugin/Services/. Everything touching AutoCAD runs through on the main thread.

member.summary:
Chooses and starts the speech recognizer, all off the UI thread:
Windows privacy: microphone blocked for desktop apps -> explained, nothing is opened.
Windows dictation (, best quality, live text) unless "Online speech recognition" is known to be off.
Otherwise, or when dictation cannot start (online speech off, no internet, language not installed, Windows Runtime not available): the offline Windows Speech Recognition engine (), with a hint why. When neither works, the dictation problem is reported (it names the Windows setting to change).
No microphone and a blocked microphone are reported at once (the other engine would fail the same way).
